proof_summary: Take \(\epsilon=\tfrac12\) and choose an arbitrarily large prime \(p\); among the positive integers at most \(p\), only \(1\) and \(p\) have no prime factors other than \(p\), so the relevant count is \(2\). Choosing \(p\ge 81\) gives \(\sqrt{\log p}>2\), contradicting the asserted eventual lower bound.
